newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to pull out last Chechnya troops by Jan 25.
newsitem.headline: Russia to pull out last Chechnya troops by Jan 25.

text.p: Russia's Defence Ministry will start pulling out its last troops from breakaway Chechnya on December 1 and the withdrawal will end by January 25, the eve of planned elections there, Interfax news agency said on Wednesday.

The decision follows a pledge made by President Boris Yeltsin last weekend to withdraw Russia's two remaining units from the region, where Moscow failed to defeat separatists in a 21-month-long bloody war.

Interfax, quoting an unnamed source in the army's general staff, said the remaining troops numbered about 6,000. The ministry will also remove 2,000 armoured vehicles, four tonnes of supplies and 400 tonnes of military equipment, it added.
Russia has already withdrawn the bulk of its troops from Chechnya following an August 31 peace treaty that deferred a decision on the region's final political status for five years.
But Moscow had wanted to leave two units permanently in Chechnya -- one from the Defence Ministry and another from the Interior Ministry.
Yeltsin's surprise announcement that they would also be withdrawn sparked anger among his communist and nationalist opponents in the State Duma lower house of parliament.
They plan to hold an extraordinary parliamentary session on Friday to discuss the issue, arguing that by withdrawing the troops Yeltsin is sanctioning Chechen independence.
They have threatened to try to impeach Yeltsin -- a long drawn-out procedure which has little chance of success -- or to call for a no-confidence vote in the government.
The brigade being withdrawn will be restationed in the southern Russian city of Budennovsk, where scores of people were killed in June last year when Chechen rebels took hostages at a local hospital.

The incident forced Moscow to negotiate a ceasefire with the rebels in Chechnya, where tens of thousands of people, mostly civilians, had been killed since Russian troops were sent into the region in December 1994.
Elections to set up a post-war administration in Chechnya are scheduled for January 27.

Chechen separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev has already said he plans to run for the presidency and other candidates are likely to surface after the official launch of the election campaign on Wednesday.
